chapter: Chicago, Virginia Ravens and the northern territory bands
title: The Toledo gang: Tatum, Teddy Wilson and friends
summary: Tatum, Teddy Wilson, Barefield and other young musicians ran around Toledo's joints after work, jamming and drinking moonshine.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: How did Teddy Wilson get there?

He was there. I don't know how he got there but he was there. So Teddy -- we had a good gang. It was Teddy Wilson, Art Tatum and Art was playing at Nobles, Teddy was playing the Chateau de France, and myself and another saxophone player named George White. He's Skippy White's father, the drummer here. And there was a tenor player out of Detroit named Adams. And then Ben Smith --not Ben Smith but Ben Richardson, who was clarinet player. And he's here in New York now. We had a little gang that we used to run around and hit all the joints at night and drink moonshine, and you know.
So this is how -- and played, you know. Jam and play and all hang out together. And that's when Art and I became very good friends, and Teddy Wilson. We all were good friends.
